newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money firms up, gilts inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money firms up, gilts inactive.

text.p: Indian call money hardened to close Thursday in the 6.0-6.5 percent range on reduced supply of funds against the opening 4.5-5.0 percent, dealers said.
They said call money rates firmed up as funds supply seemed to have reduced in the market and some lenders chose the opportunity to drive up rates.

"The Unit Trust of India (UTI) was not in the market," said a dealer. "This reduced the availability of funds to some extent. Further some lenders seem to have parked funds in on-tap treasury bills with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The overall supply of funds seems to have come down a bit."
Dealers said investments in on-tap treasury bills were inevitable as they offered a higher rate of return, 4.6 percent, than the sub four percent rates seen in the market last week.
Dealers said there was little activity in the government securities market as hardening call rates drove buyers away.
"There are only sellers in the market," said a dealer. "With rates tightening, market players are not prepared to lock up funds in securities. There were deals in only two stocks today."
The 13.50 percent 1998 government of India stock was traded on Thursday at 102 rupees against its last traded price of 102.50 rupees, they said.
The 13.55 percent 2001 stock was traded at 100.27 rupees against 100.33.
There were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit, dealers said.
